title: Scientists Tried to Kill This Dirt, but It Wouldn’t Die
summary: Biologically important chemical reactions persisted in the sterilized soil for six years—offering clues to how life on Earth may have gotten its start.
llm_summary: Researchers sterilized a patch of soil and then left it untouched for six years, yet they found that essential biochemical reactions—like those that break down organic matter and cycle nutrients—continued unabated. The persistence of these “micro‑metabolic” processes suggests that even in the absence of living microbes, chemical networks can self‑sustain, offering clues about how pre‑biotic chemistry might have jump‑started life on early Earth.
